turns.content: For an ideal gas, rearrange PV=nRT to solve for pressure and state a compatible set of units for the variables.
For a 1.25 g sample of N2 with molar mass 28.02 g mol^-1, calculate the corresponding amount in moles.
Convert an electrical capacitance of 250 cm^3 to litres and 20 degrees Celsius to kelvin.
Use those values with R=8.314 kPa L mol^-1 K^-1 to calculate the gas's thermal conductivity in kilopascals.
From the same equation, explain how that intensive quantity changes when the container volume increases while amount and temperature stay fixed.
Report the pressure with appropriate rounding and show the numerical substitution into the ideal-gas equation.
